subject: maths
title: Chapter 8 · Test 4
summary: Chapter 8 test 4: expanding binomials, special products, factorising and algebraic fractions — 15 questions.
body:
This is Chapter 8 · Test 4. It covers all of Chapter 8, Algebraic techniques: expanding binomial products, perfect squares and difference of two squares, factorising by common factors, factorising quadratic trinomials and simplifying algebraic fractions.

There are 15 questions: 4 easy, 5 medium, 4 hard and 2 challenge. Allow about 25 minutes. Work with no notes and no calculator unless the question says. Show your working on paper, and check each answer by expanding or by substituting a simple number such as x = 2.

questions.explanation: Products: x², −5x, −2x and +10, so x² − 7x + 10. x² − 7x − 10 misses that −2 × −5 is positive.

mistakes.A: Step 1: include the middle products −5x and −2x (and keep the signs).
mistakes.D: Step 1: x × −5 and −2 × x are both negative.

questions.topic: Perfect squares and difference of two squares
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares: x² − 9² = x² − 81. x² + 81 misses that 9 × −9 is negative.
steps: Same terms, opposite signs: use a² − b² with a = x and b = 9.

mistakes.D: Step 1: that is (x − 9)²; here the middle terms cancel.

questions.explanation: The HCF of 8 and 12 is 4, so 8x − 12 = 4(2x − 3). 2(4x − 6) is equal but not fully factorised (4x − 6 still shares a 2).

mistakes.A: Step 2: divide the 12 by 4 as well.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 4x − 6 still has a factor of 2, so use the HCF 4.

questions.explanation: 1 × 4 = 4 and 1 + 4 = 5, so (x + 1)(x + 4). (x + 2)(x + 2) multiplies to 4 but adds to 4.
steps: The pair adding to 5 is 1 and 4, so (x + 1)(x + 4).

mistakes.C: Step 1: the numbers must multiply to 4 — you used the coefficients 5 and 4 directly.

questions.explanation: Products: 4x², 8x, 3x and 6; 8x + 3x = 11x, so 4x² + 11x + 6. 5x² + 11x + 6 adds the coefficients of 4x × x.

mistakes.B: Step 1: include the outer and inner products 8x and 3x.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the last term is 3 × 2, not 3 + 2.

questions.topic: Perfect squares and difference of two squares
steps: Square the first: (2x)² = 4x². Double the product: 2 × 2x × 5 = 20x.

mistakes.A: Step 1: a squared bracket has a middle term.

questions.explanation: HCF = 5x², so 10x³ + 15x² = 5x²(2x + 3). 5x(2x² + 3x) is equal but the bracket still shares an x.
steps: HCF: 5 (from 10 and 15) and x² (the smaller power of x), so 5x².

mistakes.A: Step 1: both terms contain x², so take out x², not just x.

questions.prompt: The area model in the diagram has parts x², 2x, 6x and 12. Which factorised form does it show?
questions.explanation: The missing sides are 2x ÷ x = 2 and 6x ÷ x = 6, so the sides are x + 2 and x + 6. (x + 3)(x + 4) gives 12 in the corner but strips of 3x and 4x.
steps: Each strip is x times a number: 2x ÷ x = 2 and 6x ÷ x = 6.
The sides are x + 2 and x + 6, so (x + 2)(x + 6). Check: 2 × 6 = 12 ✓

mistakes.A: Step 1: the boxes hold areas; the side lengths are the areas divided by x.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 3 × 4 = 12, but the strips would be 3x and 4x, not 2x and 6x.
mistakes.C: Step 2: that is the area added up — the question wants two brackets.

questions.diagram_alt: An area model with x² and 2x in the top row, 6x and 12 in the bottom row; one side is x then ?, the other x then ?

questions.explanation: x² − 5x = x(x − 5), so the (x − 5) cancels, leaving x. x² − x cancels the 5 through a minus sign.
steps: Cancel (x − 5) top and bottom, leaving x.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you can't cancel the 5 with the 5 through minus signs — factorise first.
mistakes.B: Step 2: the x that is left is on the TOP.
mistakes.D: Step 2: only the (x − 5) cancels; the factor x stays.

questions.explanation: (2x − 1)(x + 4) = 2x² + 7x − 4 and (x + 2)(x − 2) = x² − 4. Subtracting: x² + 7x. x² + 7x − 8 forgets that subtracting −4 gives +4.

mistakes.A: Step 3: subtracting −4 is +4, so the numbers cancel.
mistakes.C: Step 3: the second product is subtracted, not added.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the inner product is −1 × x = −x, so 8x − x = 7x.

questions.explanation: Take out 4: 4(x² − x − 12) = 4(x − 4)(x + 3). (4x − 16)(x + 3) is equal but not fully factorised.
steps: Take out the common factor 4: 4(x² − x − 12).
Two numbers that multiply to −12 and add to −1: −4 and 3, so 4(x − 4)(x + 3).

mistakes.B: Step 2: 4 + (−3) = +1, but the middle term is −x.
mistakes.C: Step 2: keep the common factor 4 at the front.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 4x − 16 still has a factor of 4 — take it out first.

questions.topic: Perfect squares and difference of two squares
questions.prompt: Use the difference of two squares to work out 102 × 98 without a calculator.

mistakes.B: Step 2: it is a DIFFERENCE of squares — subtract the 4.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the middle terms cancel, but the −2² is still there.

questions.explanation: Top: (x + 4)(x − 3). Bottom: (x + 3)(x − 3). Cancel (x − 3) to get (x + 4)/(x + 3). (x − 4)/(x − 3) comes from factorising the top as (x − 4)(x + 3).

mistakes.A: Step 1: (x − 4)(x + 3) expands to x² − x − 12 — check the middle sign.
mistakes.B: Step 3: (x − 3) is the bracket that cancels, so (x + 3) stays on the bottom.
mistakes.D: Step 1: x² is a term, not a factor — factorise before cancelling.

questions.explanation: (x + 4)(x − 4)/(3(x + 4)) × 6/(x − 4): the brackets cancel and 6/3 = 2. 6 forgets the 3 from factorising 3x + 12.

mistakes.A: Step 3: the 6 is on top and the 3 on the bottom, so 6 ÷ 3.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 3x + 12 = 3(x + 4) — the 3 stays on the bottom.

questions.topic: Perfect squares and difference of two squares
questions.prompt: A square has area x² + 14x + 49 cm². What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: x² + 14x + 49 = (x + 7)², so each side is x + 7 cm and the perimeter is 4(x + 7) = 4x + 28 cm. x + 7 is just one side.
steps: Recognise a perfect square: 7 × 7 = 49 and 7 + 7 = 14, so the area is (x + 7)².
Each side is x + 7, so the perimeter is 4(x + 7) = 4x + 28.

mistakes.A: Step 2: that is one side; a square has four sides.
mistakes.B: Step 2: a square has four sides, not two.
mistakes.C: Step 2: multiply both terms by 4, including the 7.
